clues.title: Bollard: Bollard
text: Hungarian bollards are black-and-white, wedge-shaped, and typically have a red reflector at the front, and a white reflector at the back. (Croatian bollards are similar but the black part with reflector is closer to the top).
Note: Can appear in slovakia

clues.title: Pole: Holey pole
text: Concrete holey poles with medium-sized holes going all the way to the bottom are common. They are similar to those in Poland and Romania, but Polish poles have holes that don't go all the way to the top or bottom, and Romanian poles are usually wider and painted white at the bottom.

clues.title: Sign: 4 Bolt Signs
text: Hungarian signs are usually bolted to the sign post using four bolts, going through the sign, in the shape of a tall rectangle.
This is not common in any other Eastern European countries.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: Poles
text: The most common type of utility pole in Hungary is a concrete holey pole, with relatively thin holes going all the way down to the ground.
**In eastern Europe, Poland and Romania also commonly use holey poles:**
Polish holey poles typically do not have holes down by the ground, and tend to be relatively thin.
Romanian holey poles normally either have much wider, or much taller holes.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Mountains
text: While the southeastern parts of Hungary are extremely flat, with almost no noticeable hills, the northern and western parts mainly consist of forested hills and mountains. The tallest mountains are found in the north, while the southwestern mountains are generally slightly lower.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Puszta Grasslands
text: Unlike most of the Hungarian plains, which is almost entirely cultivated land, the Puszta, centred around Hortobágy National Park, mainly consists of barren and wet, natural grasslands.

clues.title: Architecture: Red Tiles Roofs & Light Colors
text: Hungarian houses are typically made of stone, painted in a light colour and almost always with red tiled roofs.
Suburban houses are typically only one storeyed, while more central houses may be taller.
Houses in town and city centres are often fairly old but well-kept.

clues.title: Language: Hungarian
text: Hungarian is a Ugric language that is unrelated to all its surrounding languages. It has a unique look, with a large number of acute accents (**Á, É, Í, Ó, Ú**), umlauts (**Ö, Ü**), and long words. The letters **Ő** and **Ű**, with **double** acute accents, are unique to the language.
The Hungarian name for street is **utca**. The word **út** is also used for bigger roads. No other language shares this name.
NOTE: Hungarian is widely spoken is parts of neighboring countries, notably Romania and Slovakia.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
